newsitem.title: CANADA: Magna to buy Tricom for C$72 mln.
newsitem.headline: Magna to buy Tricom for C$72 mln.

text.p: Magna International Inc said on Monday it entered into an agreement to acquire 100 percent of the shares of Tricom Group Holdings Ltd for a purchase price of about C$72 million.
The deal is expected to close by about May 23.

Tricom and its subsidiaries operate three wholly owned manufacturing facilities in the United Kingdom which design, engineer and manufacture complete seats, seat frames and other seating components for the automotive industry.

Magna said Tricom, whose principal customers include Ford Motor Co, Rover, General Motors and a number of other original equipment manufacturers in the U.K., is expected to have annualized sales in calendar 1997 of about C$140 million.

Magna Vice-Chairman Bill Fike said the acquisition of Tricom, as well as the recent North American acquisition of Douglas & Lomason are major steps in Magna's strategy to become a leading supplier of seating systems to the global automotive industry.

"This acquisition enables Magna to significantly expand its seating capability to Europe and, together with its acquisition last year of the automotive operations of Marley Plc ( ) and the recent acquisition of Georg Naher GmbH, significantly strengthens Magna's complete interior systems capability in Europe and further enhances its position as a major full service supplier to the global automotive industry," Fike said in a statement.
Magna also announced that it has completed the previously announced acquisition of 100% of GNG, subject to German anti-trust approval, for approximately C$44 million.
